_about: The one list of forecast systems and how they are grouped. scripts/build.py renders the forecast systems table on the accuracy page from it and ships it in config.js, where the scorecard grid takes its row groups and row order from the same list. Change the grouping or the order here and both follow. `id` is the system's id in the accuracy files; `ens` is its entry in calibration.json's ensembles; a row may carry either or both.

groups.title: Prediction market
groups.note: The system every other row is compared against.

systems.name: ForecastEx
systems.what: Daily contracts on each city’s high and low temperature. The ladder of Yes prices across strikes is a probability distribution for the settle.

groups.title: Raw numerical weather prediction models
groups.note: Physics models that step the atmosphere forward in time. Their output applies to a grid box rather than the exact point where a station sits.

systems.name: European Model
systems.what: ECMWF’s global model, the IFS, as one deterministic run. Before live capture began the record uses ECMWF’s 0.25° open data from the forecast archive, and from then on a data provider’s high-resolution series, whose grid spacing could not be confirmed.
systems.grid: 0.25°, about 25 km, in the archive, not confirmed for the live series

systems.name: European Ensemble Mean
systems.what: Described by the data provider as the average of ECMWF’s 51-member ensemble, which could not be independently confirmed. Only its mean is used here.

systems.name: American Model
systems.what: NOAA’s Global Forecast System. Before live capture began the record comes from a forecast archive that returns HRRR within 48 hours of the run.

systems.name: American Ensemble
systems.what: NOAA’s Global Ensemble Forecast System, 31 members.

systems.name: German Model
systems.what: ICON, the global model of Germany’s weather service.

systems.name: German Ensemble
systems.what: ICON’s global ensemble, 40 members.

systems.name: Canadian Model
systems.what: GEM, the model of Environment and Climate Change Canada, as a seamless series that uses its regional and high-resolution configurations at US stations.

systems.name: Canadian Ensemble
systems.what: Canada’s global ensemble, 21 members.

systems.name: UK Model
systems.what: The Met Office Unified Model, run globally.

systems.name: French Model
systems.what: ARPEGE, the global model of Météo-France.

systems.name: Japanese Model
systems.what: The Global Spectral Model of the Japan Meteorological Agency.

systems.name: HRRR
systems.what: NOAA’s High-Resolution Rapid Refresh, covering the contiguous United States.

groups.title: Numerical weather prediction with model output statistics
groups.note: Physics model output corrected station by station against what the models got wrong in the past.

systems.name: National Blend of Models
systems.what: NOAA’s calibrated blend of many models, the starting point for the Weather Service’s own forecast.

systems.name: Blend MOS
systems.what: The station text bulletin of the National Blend of Models.

systems.name: Aviation Forecast
systems.what: LAMP, statistical guidance refreshed with the latest observations.

systems.name: GFS MOS
systems.what: Statistical guidance built on the American Model alone, with no forecaster editing.

systems.name: NAM MOS
systems.what: Statistical guidance built on NOAA’s North American Mesoscale model.

systems.name: German Statistical Model
systems.what: MOSMIX, which combines and corrects the German and European models.
systems.grid: The settlement airport’s station in DWD’s list, which lacks Buckley Field, Houston Hobby and Chicago Midway

groups.title: Human forecasting systems
groups.note: Forecasters editing model guidance with their own judgment.

systems.name: National Weather Service
systems.what: The official public forecast from the National Digital Forecast Database, which forecasters edit starting from the National Blend of Models. Its high is a daytime maximum for 7 AM to 7 PM local standard time and its low an overnight minimum for 7 PM to 8 AM, assigned to the morning the night ends, while the contracts settle on the calendar day.
systems.updates: About twice a day, amended as needed

groups.title: AI systems
groups.note: Models trained on decades of past weather rather than stepping physical equations forward.

systems.name: European AI Ensemble Mean
systems.what: AIFS, ECMWF’s machine-learning forecasting system. Live, it is the 51-member ensemble, whose mean is scored as one value and whose members’ spread as a distribution. Before live capture began the forecast archive holds its single deterministic run.
